findings.reason: §4's text and its done-when ("§4 therefore extends that engine", "that branch is retired") should be re-pointed at what remains — the JT-60SA catalogue and the OP1/OP2 identity assertions — so a dispatched worker does not go to extend an engine that already carries the extension.
findings.text: §4 presents the `StoreEngine.open` store-layout extension and the probe-angle machine-branch retirement as work the plan will do, but both are already present in the reviewed tree: `transform_engine.py:169`/`:282` already receive `store_layout` and refuse/read `static-over-map`, and `description_reader.py:144` branches on `catalog.probe_angle_source == "acquisition-address"`, with no `machine == "mast"` branch anywhere — so §4's account of the mechanism it "extends" and of a machine branch it "retires" describes landed machinery.

findings.reason: the plan names the owning files, gives the dependency-weight reason (codex's neo4j/fastmcp/lxml/pypdf requirement set on ambix's runtime path, which the map-persistence decision rules out) and defers a shared core to a second facility needing remote execution — the honest decline the item asks for, not a fork that ignored its owner.
findings.text: §3 forks codex's remote layer (`imas_codex/remote/scripts/enumerate_edas.py`, `executor.py`, `ssh_worker.py`, `serialization.py`) into ambix rather than importing or extracting a shared core.

findings.reason: §6 already states the loader boundary is a canonical record contract (grid, psi, axis, boundary) that the DIII-D loader maps onto and the kernel reads, which is exactly the extension of `challenge/loader.py`'s `ChallengeShot`/`EfitLabels.psirz`, so the plan's stated design already covers the coupling.
findings.text: §6 generalises `measure_diiid_convention` to take an equilibrium record through a loader while the head of `convention.py` still reads DIII-D corpus keys (`efit_grid_R`, `efit_psirz`, `efit_z_axis`) directly in `_axis_and_boundary`/`_integrated_current`, so the loader boundary is described but `_axis_and_boundary` and `_integrated_current` retain corpus-key coupling on the DIII-D side.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the proposed new modules each hide substantial behaviour behind a single small surface: `data/eddb_remote.py` (one batch-fetch function) over ssh transport plus the remote script, `data/eddb.py` (one cache writer) over the raw-unit zarr layout and the series-letter/int shot-identity refusal, `data/selene_deck.py` (one converter entry point) over four deck grammars and five IDS writers, `data/tokamap_export.py` (one public function) over the group-scoped collapse of unit × sign × COCOS into `scale`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the recurring duplicate classes are all routed to their owners: path resolution to `data/paths.py` (`JT60SA_ROOT` beside `MIRROR_ROOT`), the frozen shot set to `spine_bench/shots.py`, the artifact pins to `gs/artifact_resolution.py`, and probe-angle sourcing to `description_reader.py` via a catalogue declaration. The single cross-repo fork is filed below.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — supplied counts public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; no section adds to any of these families, so none needs to name a retirement or merge.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites and the code confirms every owner it extends: codex's remote layer (`imas_codex/remote/scripts/enumerate_edas.py`, `executor.py`, `ssh_worker.py`, `serialization.py`), the MAST machinery (`load_packaged_signal_map`, `VirtualZarrView`, `cocos_convention.score_convention`, `challenge/loader.py`, `challenge/convention._integrated_current`), and the spine route (`gs/artifact_resolution.py`, `gs/machine_selection.ArtifactMachineSelector`, `spine_bench/machine_artifact_arm.MachineArtifactGeometrySource`, `eval/efit_referee.read_efit_geometry`'s loader seam). One clause is stale — see the finding.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one wrapper-shaped addition, §7's EQDB reader, is explicitly "one remote script and one fetch entry beside the §3 extractor's, using its transport and cache rather than a second path", and §3's forked remote extractor is not a wrapper over codex but a deliberate small re-implementation carrying a stated dependency-weight rationale.
